# BFS across temporal events: state is (node, time)
# We can start at 303 at time t when it sends to x; initial state is (recipient, t)
# But better to represent frontier as events (sender, recipient, t). We'll queue events reachable.

# Build mapping from sender to list of (t, recipient)
# For quick transition, for a given node cur_node and time t_prev, find outgoing events of cur_node with t>t_prev and t<=t_prev+W
import bisect
# prebuild list of times per sender
times_by_sender={u:[tt for tt,_ in lst] for u,lst in out_by_sender.items() if lst}

# find temporal paths from each start event until reach recipient 1293
paths=[]
for t0,first_recipient in starts:
    # initial event: 303 -> first_recipient at t0
    # track visited states (node,time) to avoid loops
    q=deque()
    q.append((first_recipient,t0,[ (303,first_recipient,t0) ]))
    visited=set()
    visited.add((first_recipient,t0))
    while q:
        node,time,trace = q.popleft()
        # check if the last event delivered to 1293
        if node==1293:
            paths.append(trace)
            continue
        # look for outgoing events from node after time
        lst=out_by_sender.get(node,[])
        if not lst: continue
        times=[tt for tt,_ in lst]
        i=bisect.bisect_right(times,time)
        # iterate events with t in (time, time+W]
        while i<len(times) and times[i]-time<=W:
            t2=times[i]
            v=lst[i][1]
            state=(v,t2)
            if state not in visited:
                visited.add(state)
                q.append((v,t2, trace+[(node,v,t2)]))
            i+=1

print('found_paths_count', len(paths))
for p in paths:
    print('path:')
    for e in p:
